learning_outcomes.text: Describe the basic operation of gas turbine engines, steam power cycles, combined cycles, and internal combustion reciprocating engines.
Describe the parts, components, and fundamental devices of gas turbine engines, steam power cycles, combined cycles, and internal combustion reciprocating engines.
Perform thermodynamic analysis of gas turbine engines, steam power cycles, combined cycles, and internal combustion reciprocating engines.

Identify the most important operating parameters of gas turbine engines, steam power cycles, combined cycles, and internal combustion reciprocating engines, and establish the values of these parameters that optimize their operation.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to thermal machines and engines. Classification. Applications
Introduction. Classification. Reciprocating volumetric compressors. Rotary volumetric compressors.

Introduction. Classification. Spark ignition engines (SI) and compression ignition engines (CI). Four-stroke (4S) and two-stroke (2S) engines. Fundamental parameters (indicated and effective). Thermodynamic analysis. Characteristic curves. Equivalent air cycles. Constructive elements.

Introduction. Energy balance. Determination of thermal and mechanical losses. Engine cooling and thermal management. Lubrication. Admission and exhaust processes in 2S and 4S IC engines. Volumetric efficiency. Justification of supercharging. Types of supercharging. Turbocharging. Combustion in SI engines. Combustion in CI engines. Characteristics of fuels used in CI and SI engines. Injection systems. Mechanisms of pollutant emission formation. Reduction of pollutant emissions.
Introduction. Fundamental equation of the turbomachine. Turbomachine structure. Definition of staging. Classification of thermal turbomachines: axial and radial. Efficiency.

Thermodynamic analysis of steady-flow combustion. Operating cycles of gas turbine engines. Simple cycle gas turbine. Modifications. Aero-derivative gas turbine. Basic parameters. Exergetic analysis. Technological aspects and applications of gas turbine engines.

Justification. Gas turbine-steam cycle combined cycle with a single pressure level. Heat recovery steam generators. Thermodynamic analysis. Gas turbine-steam cycle combined cycle with multiple pressure levels. Other combined cycles.
Field practice - Visit to a thermal power plant (5 hours)

assessment_methods.method: Group oral presentation of practical activities

assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, the final grade is calculated as CF = 0.4*EvC1 + 0.15*EvC2 + 0.45*EvC3, requiring a minimum score of 4/10 in all activities; otherwise, the final grade is 'Fail' with the lowest numerical activity score. For single evaluation (85% written exam, 15% oral presentation), a minimum of 4.5/10 in the written exam and 4/10 in the oral presentation are required. If a student does not attend activities accounting for at least 50% of the continuous evaluation, they are marked 'Not Presented'. Students who did not perform practices during the semester must take a practice exam before the written exam and achieve a minimum of 4.0.
